newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Thistle shares face prickly outlook - NZPA.
newsitem.headline: Thistle shares face prickly outlook - NZPA.

text.p: Brierley Investments' Thistle Hotels could further disappoint as share price support from Merrill Lynch lapses on Monday, the New Zealand Press Association reported.
Under the British sharemarket rules, a lead broker of a float can support a share price for 30 days following listing.
But failure of Merrill Lynch to keep Thistle above its 170p listing level has raised fears of a further slump in price.
The latest closing price for the British hotel chain was 169p. On its debut at the beginning of October, Thistle briefly touched a high of 176p before heavy selling came out, pushing it back to 172p.
Brokers said at the time that it might have dropped below 170p on its first day if not for the support of Merrill Lynch.
Thistle's lack of performance has disappointed many stags, who had been hoping for at least a 10 percent profit from the much-hyped asset.
Failure of British institutions to support the float was said to be the main reason for its lack of success.
Thistle's poor showing was against a backdrop of the London sharemarket trading at around its all-time high and the likes of the hotel group Millennium and Copthorne appreciating strongly.
Raymond Webb, of broker ANZ Securities, said that without the help of Merrill Lynch the Thistle share price was likely to come under further pressure in the short term.
Thistle remains a major asset for BIL, which has retained 80 percent of its holding.
A 10p movement in Thistle's price equated to around 2c in BIL's price, Webb said.
The poor showing of Thistle had already been reflected in the BIL price. BIL's share price has slipped 5c over the week. At 130c it was now equal to BIL's asset backing.
Webb expected that once the weak holders in Thistle had got out it should trade closer to its book value of 230p a share.
